title: Condensed trace summary mode interaction notes
content:
Summary:

This is a working notes doc for a new "Condensed Trace Summary" mode in the trace viewer. The goal: give fast, scannable overviews of long traces by automatically collapsing low-signal spans and surfacing important span groups, anomalies, and cost/latency hotspots. This mode sits alongside Full Waterfall and Compact Timeline as a 3rd viewing mode users can toggle.

Why we need it:
- Customers repeatedly ask for a way to quickly triage 1000+ span traces without losing context.
- Current "compact" only reduces row height; it doesn't semantically collapse noise (health checks, client retries, repeated library spans).
- Shift left: many ops tasks are pattern-detection (e.g. repeated N+1 calls, ORM spikes) which are easier if repeated patterns are shown as single aggregated lanes.

Key goals / constraints:
- Preserve temporal accuracy (start/end alignment) even when spans are aggregated.
- Allow fast expansion/collapse with keyboard and click; state should be shareable via URL (expanded set encoded).
- Aggregation heuristics should be auditable (hover shows "why these spans are grouped").
- Must not lose high-cardinality attributes on collapse (quick peek + copy-to-clipboard available).
- Performance: condensation step should run client-side incrementally; avoid blocking main thread for 5000-span traces.

Wireframe & layout notes (sketch-to-text):
- Left column: condensed lane map (mini-legend) with lane-level toggles (service / library / db / browser).
- Center: timeline pane with 3 levels: Full rows (expanded), Condensed lanes (aggregate rows), Mini-waterfall sparkline (in-lane).
  - Each condensed lane shows: aggregated label (e.g. "DB calls (x32)"), total time bar (sum or max depending on user setting), representative span chip (short message), and anomaly badge (if any).
  - Sparkline shows distribution of start times across the group; hovering shows a small histogram tooltip.
- Right: details panel (when a condensed lane or representative span is selected) with tabs: Summary | Top-instance | Raw spans (paginated) | Related traces.
- Top bar: mode toggle [Full | Condensed | Compact], keyboard hint (press "C" to toggle condensed), filter pill set persists across modes.

Interactions and microcopy:
- Hover condensed lane -> tooltip: "Grouped 32 spans across 6 hosts. Reason: repeated client retries. Click to expand."
- Expand interaction: click chevron or press Enter while focused. Expanding in-place will insert the member spans below the condensed row with smooth height animation. Collapsing removes them.
- Peek: hover the rep span chip and press Space to open a transient overlay showing the top 5 instances (no DOM insert).
- Keyboard: Up/Down to move lane focus, Right to expand, Left to collapse, F to focus filter input, / to open quick search.
- URL state: ?mode=condensed&expanded=[laneId:0,laneId:3]&focus=span-347

Aggregation heuristics (initial proposal):
- Primary keys used to group: [service, span.kind, operation name normalized, host/instance, library fingerprint].
- Group when: same operation name AND consecutive spans from same upstream parent OR repeated occurrences separated by < 5s and same attributes.
- Special-case: group health-check pings and edge-router access logs by pattern-match and mark collapsed-by-default.
- User override whitelist: if user has pinned span attributes (via filter) those spans should not be aggregated.
- Representative span selection: pick the 90th-percentile duration span or the earliest errored instance. Show label: "rep: >250ms (p90)".

UX signals to expose grouping rationale:
- Each condensed lane has a small "i" icon; hover shows bullets: number of spans, time range, grouping rule matched, sample instance id.
- Click "Audit" in detail panel to open a side-by-side list view of member spans with checkboxes so users can ungroup specific members.

Filtering & discoverability:
- Quick filters in condensed mode: "show noisy lanes only", "errors only", "top N by total time", "top N by count".
- Filters should update lane badges live (e.g., error count) and dim collapsed lanes that don't match.
- Provide suggested filter chips based on aggregated signals ("Show 3 lanes with spikes >200ms").

Performance considerations / implementation notes:
- Do grouping in a WebWorker and stream results back as lanes are ready. Fall back to incremental single-thread processing if worker unavailable.
- Keep a lightweight index of attribute hashes to avoid repeated deep object comparisons.
- For very large traces (>2000 spans) default to sampling group membership on first render and fetch full membership lazily for the details panel.
- Cache condensation choices per session; offer opt-out in settings for determinism.

Accessibility & a11y:
- Condensed lanes should be keyboard-focusable; expansion state exposed via ARIA-expanded.
- Provide high-contrast mode for badges and ensure sparkline has semantic alt text in screen-reader mode.
- Voiceover hint in top bar: "Trace viewer in condensed mode. Press Right to expand selected lane."

Metrics we will track (proposal):
- Time to first meaningful render of condensed lanes (target < 350ms for 500-span trace).
- % of traces where user expands at least one condensed lane (engagement).
- Time-to-first-insight (click to error/slow span) vs baseline waterfall.
- CPU usage on client-side condensation vs compact mode.

Rollout plan / experiment idea:
- Phase 0: internal beta for SE + SRE teams behind feature flag. Collect feedback on grouping heuristics.
- Phase 1: 10% of customers, A/B test: default mode remains Full, but "Condensed" is suggested in a banner for traces > 500 spans. Measure discovery and mean time to triage.
- Phase 2: make Condensed first-class with user preference persisted.

Backlog (groomed tasks / rough estimates):
- UX high-fidelity mockups and click-through (2d) - owner: Maya - 3d
- Grouping algorithm prototype (webworker) + benchmark harness - owner: Diego - 5d - JIRA-1255
- Representative span selection heuristics and spec - owner: Ava - 2d
- Details panel design + API contract for paginated raw spans - owner: Liam - 3d - JIRA-1260
- Keyboard navigation and ARIA - owner: SRE/Accessibility - 2d
- Unit + e2e tests for expansion state persistence - owner: Eng QA - 3d
- Telemetry events and Graphite/Grafana dashboards - owner: Observability - 2d

Open questions / discussion points (notes to self):
- When aggregating, should the aggregate time show SUM or MAX? SUM emphasizes cumulative cost; MAX emphasizes critical path. Maybe user toggle with clear tooltips.
- How to reconcile parent-child relationships when a child is grouped but parent remains expanded? Need a visual connector or translucent link.
- Branding: call it "Condensed Summary" vs "Aggregate Mode" vs "Rollup Mode" — what maps best to user mental model?
- Should snapshot/export include collapsed state and include member-span ids? We should include both collapsed and raw lists to make debugging reproducible.

Immediate next steps:
- Create initial Figma frames for the three-stage layout (lane map, center condensed rows, detail panel). (Maya)
- Diego to spike a worker-based grouping prototype against a 2000-span synthetic trace and report perf numbers today.
- Sync with Observability team on proposed telemetry.

Small TODO list (raw):
- [ ] add example JSON of condensed output shape for API (flat list of lanes + sample ids)
- [ ] draft help doc text for product docs: "When to use Condensed mode"
- [ ] list of negative aggregation examples (what we must never collapse)


END - rough draft for internal grooming. Lots of open choices. Ping in #product-console or DM if you want to riff on heuristics.
